title: Completion-at-point provider exclusivity

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: `completion-at-point-functions' providers are queried through hook wrapping; `:exclusive no' changes whether later providers are tried after a failed prefix match.
hypothesis: An exclusive first CAPF with no matching candidate should prevent the second CAPF from being queried; marking it `:exclusive no' should allow the second CAPF to answer.
minimal_fixture: Two synthetic CAPFs over the prefix `zz': the first offers only `aa', the second offers `zz-top'.
predicted_behavior: Provider ordering is not a simple merge: the exclusive first provider blocks fallback, while a non-exclusive first provider permits fallback.
observed_behavior: exclusive-calls=("first") exclusive-result=(#[nil ((progn (setq exclusive-calls (cons "first" exclusive-calls)) (list (point-min) (point-max) (list "aa")))) ((exclusive-calls "first"))] 1 3 ("aa")) nonexclusive-calls=("first" "second") nonexclusive-result=(#[nil ((progn (setq nonexclusive-calls (cons "second" nonexclusive-calls)) (list (point-min) (point-max) (list "zz-top")))) ((nonexclusive-calls "first" "second"))] 1 3 ("zz-top"))

independent_checks.name: fallback result came from second provider

counterexample: A FIM overlay that assumes all completion sources are merged can fight CAPF ownership and show stale or duplicate candidates.
derived_gym_requirement: Completion integration must record provider order, replacement range, exclusivity, and whether the model path is separate from or participates in CAPF.
